guide.title: How VAT verification works
guide.subtitle: What the plugin checks, when, and what the answers mean.

start.title: What it does
start.text: The plugin checks a buyer's tax ID: a Polish NIP on the Ministry of Finance white list (and in GUS with a key), an EU VAT number in VIES. Every answer is stored with the register's request ID, so you can prove the check was made.

registers.title: The registers
registers.text:
White list: free, about 100 requests a day; shows VAT status and bank accounts.
GUS (REGON): knows every business, not only VAT payers; needs a free key from api.stat.gov.pl.
VIES: EU VAT numbers; with your own VAT number it issues a consultation number as proof.

verdicts.title: Verdicts
verdicts.text: Active VAT payer, VAT exempt, not a VAT payer, business closed, valid EU VAT, invalid, not found, or could not verify. "Could not verify" means no register answered (down, slow or over its limit): it is never treated as invalid.

orders.title: Orders
orders.text: An order with a tax ID is verified when placed. The answer is linked to the order and the customer and shown in their Integrations cards. Answers are reused for 24 hours (cacheTtlHours).

checkout.title: Checkout
checkout.text: The storefront can check a number while the buyer types it (/store/whitelist-vat/verify) and fill in the company data. Refusing carts with an invalid number is off by default (checkout.rejectOnCompletion).

limits.title: Daily limit
limits.text: The plugin stops asking the white list after its daily limit (mf.dailyLimit, 95) and counts the day in Polish time. Add a GUS key or raise cacheTtlHours for many B2B orders a day.

demo.title: Demo mode
demo.text: demo: true makes GUS answer with sample businesses without a key. NIP 1112223332 is a closed business, 9876543210 is not found. The white list and VIES are asked as usual.
